noi_dung:
Before you begin

Choose a clean, quiet place and allow enough time to practice without rushing. Sit or stand upright, relax, and join your palms. If offering incense, prepare it before the opening liturgy and keep the altar area orderly.

Set your intention: the well-being of yourself or someone else, or remembrance of a person who has died. Have the person’s name ready for the prayer.

Step 1 · Opening liturgy

In “Recitation ritual”, find “Opening liturgy • Well-being and remembrance”. Follow the sections in order: purification of the Dharma Realm, purification of the three karmas, incense offering, praise of the Buddha, prayer, contemplation, and homage.

Recite each opening purification mantra 3 times. Recite the final invocation in the incense offering 3 times. In the prayer, replace the name placeholder with the person for whom you are practicing. Follow the bow counts printed after each homage.

Step 2 · Invocation

Continue to “Treasure Chest Seal Dhāraṇī • 21 repetitions”. Recite the opening invocation 3 times, then continue to the main dhāraṇī.

Step 3 · Recite the complete dhāraṇī

Begin with “namas tryadhvikānāṁ” and continue through the final “hūṁ hūṁ svāhā”. This whole text counts as one repetition. Repeat the entire text until you have completed 21 repetitions.

Line breaks are reading aids. Do not repeat each individual line 21 times. Recite slowly and clearly, keep a steady pace, and attend to the words. You may use the practice-mode counter to track completed repetitions.

Keeping a regular practice

If making a commitment over several days, choose a manageable daily time and keep it consistently. A commitment may run for 7, 14, 21, or 49 days, with 21 complete repetitions each day in this practice schedule.

During the commitment, emphasize vegetarian food, non-harming, purity of conduct, and moral discipline. This particular practice tradition also observes abstinence from marital sexual activity during the chosen commitment period.

When circumstances are difficult

If a suitable place or enough time is unavailable, sincerely recollect the Buddha and dedicate the merit to your loved ones. Maintain a sincere heart, do good, and choose a practice that fits your circumstances.

Benefits described in the scripture

The Treasure Chest Seal scripture presents recitation, homage, and offerings as ways to accumulate merit, purify harmful karma, and support awakening. It also describes dedicating practice to the departed with the aspiration for a favorable rebirth.

Practice together with compassion, ethical conduct, and wholesome actions.

Editorial references: the Treasure Chest Seal scripture published by Buddha Sutras • Mantras • Sanskrit; FPMT’s Four Dharmakaya Relic Mantras materials.

Opening liturgy • Well-being and remembrance

1. Purification of the Dharma Realm

Oṃ raṃ svāhā.

3 times.

2. Purification of the Three Karmas

Oṃ svabhāva śuddhāḥ sarva dharmāḥ svabhāva śuddho ’haṃ.

3 times.

3. Incense offering

With a heart of reverence, I send this cloud of incense
Throughout the ten directions, as an offering to the Three Jewels.
May I keep the path throughout my life and do good in accordance with my true nature.
Together with all beings in the Dharma Realm, I seek the compassionate protection of the Buddhas.
May the awakening mind be steadfast and the resolve to learn enduring.
May we leave the vast ocean of suffering and swiftly reach the shore of awakening.

Homage to the Incense Offering Bodhisattva, the Great Being.

3 times.

4. Praise of the Buddha

Unsurpassed King of the Dharma,
Without equal in the three realms,
Teacher of humans and celestial beings,
Compassionate father of the four kinds of birth.
In one wholehearted thought we take refuge,
Purifying the karma of three incalculable ages.
We proclaim and sing your praises
Through countless unending eons.

5. Prayer

We, your disciples, uphold the teachings of our original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha. Through reciting scriptures and mantras, praising the sacred names, and cultivating merit, we sincerely ask the Three Jewels throughout the ten directions, Śākyamuni Buddha, and all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the assembly of the Treasure Chest Seal Dhāraṇī to compassionately protect [name of the practitioner, the person who is ill, or the deceased relative or spirit]. May afflictions cease, karmic obstacles be purified, peace prevail, and suffering be left behind. May all sentient beings together complete the Buddha path.

6. Contemplation

The nature of Buddha and sentient beings is always empty and still.
Their communion is beyond conception.
Like the jeweled net of Indra, this place of practice
Reflects the brilliant light of Buddhas in all ten directions.
Before the precious throne, my form appears.
I bow my head, pay homage, and take refuge.

7. Homage to the Buddhas

With one mind I bow to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three times, the honored Dharma, and the noble Sangha: the ever-abiding Three Jewels pervading all space and the Dharma Realm.

1 bow.

With one mind I bow to Śākyamuni Buddha, teacher of this Sahā world; Maitreya Buddha of the Dragon Flower assembly; Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva of great wisdom; Samantabhadra Bodhisattva of great conduct; the Dharma-protecting Bodhisattvas; all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and noble Sangha gathered in this place of practice.

1 bow.

With one mind I bow to Amitābha Buddha, the greatly compassionate guide of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss; Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of great compassion; Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva; Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva of great vows; and the pure ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas.

1 bow.

Treasure Chest Seal Dhāraṇī • 21 repetitions

Invocation • 3 times

Homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the assembly of the Whole-Body Relic Treasure Chest Seal Dhāraṇī, the Heart Secret of All Tathāgatas.

Main dhāraṇī

Recite the complete text below 21 times. Line breaks are reading aids, not separate mantras.

namas tryadhvikānāṁ sarva tathāgatānāṁ

oṁ bhuvi-bhavana-vare

vacana-vacati suru suru dhara dhara

sarva tathāgata dhātu dhare

padmaṁ bhavati jaya vare mudre

smara tathāgata dharma-cakra pravartana vajre bodhimaṇḍālaṁkārālaṁkṛte

sarva tathāgatādhiṣṭhite

bodhaya bodhaya bodhi bodhi

budhya budhya saṁbodhani saṁbodhaya

cala cala calantu

sarvāvaraṇāni sarva pāpa vigate

huru huru sarva śoka vigate

sarva tathāgata hṛdaya vajriṇi

saṁbhāra saṁbhāra

sarva tathāgata guhya dhāraṇī-mudre

bhūte subhūte

sarva tathāgatādhiṣṭhita dhātu garbhe svāhā

samayādhiṣṭhite svāhā

sarva tathāgata hṛdaya dhātu mudre svāhā

supratiṣṭhita stūpe tathāgatādhiṣṭhite huru huru hūṁ hūṁ svāhā

oṁ sarva tathāgatoṣṇīṣa dhātu mudrāṇi

sarva tathāgata sadhātu vibhūṣitādhiṣṭhite hūṁ hūṁ svāhā
